incident-bot: PagerDuty alert -> DATABASE: high connection count on pg-primary (service=db-write). Trigger: >95% connections used, query queueing increasing. Pager: @miko (oncall).

pagerduty: Incident 8921 triggered: db-write connections_exhausted. Auto-page sent.

miko: oncall here, looking. seeing lots of short-lived spikes from api-prod, probably connection churn. paging into thread.

jamie: I can confirm. `pg_stat_activity` shows huge wait_event = 'ClientRead' and backlog on `pg_stat_io` basically queueing.

jamie: quick check:```sql
SELECT state, count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity GROUP BY state;
-- output:
-- active | 312
-- idle | 1200
-- idle in transaction | 45
```

olivia: also seeing cache pressure on redis-primary: `used_memory_peak` spiking, and `maxclients` at ~98%. TTL miss rate up ~3x -> more db hits.

cheng: any recent deploys?

miko: no deploys in last hour, traffic spike from experiment-variant B started ~10m ago.

jamie: root cause looks like connection pool exhaustion + thundering small transactions. app side not reusing pools. pg_bouncer is in transaction mode which amplifies client connections.

olivia: we're also getting increased 5xxs in front of write-heavy endpoints. support-bot earlier flagged ~1200 errors/min for PUT /notes.

support-bot: Customers impacted: ~0.8% of write requests failing, top affected tenants: acme-inc, beta-co, 12 smaller orgs. SLAs: degraded. Ticket queue getting noise.

miko: mitigation plan: 1) short-term: enable emergency pg_bouncer overflow + reduce pool_size on app side via runtime config, 2) mid-term: add one standby to absorb read-surge, 3) investigate app connection handling.

cheng: I'll do the pg_bouncer tweak. doing: `ALTER SYSTEM SET max_client_conn = 500;` (bouncer config reload) and temporarily switch pgbouncer from transaction -> session? That might help reuse but risk pooling semantics.

jamie: careful switching modes might break transactional assumptions. instead: increase pool_size for pgbouncer and enable reserve_pool to handle bursts. Command:```ini
[pgbouncer]
pool_mode = transaction
max_client_conn = 1000
default_pool_size = 200
reserve_pool_size = 50
reserve_pool_timeout = 5
```

miko: go ahead with reserve_pool change, jamie + cheng coordinate. I'll bump app-side min pool to 5 and max to 50 for the next 20m via feature-flag.

cheng: applied pgbouncer config change on pg-bouncer-1, reloaded. logs show: `NOTICE: Server reset; reserve clients available = 50`.

olivia: I scaled redis-primary one shard up + bumped maxclients in redis conf for now. cleared a few large ephemeral keys causing eviction storms.

jamie: after pgbouncer changes, `pg_stat_activity` look better.```sql
-- now:
-- active | 95
-- idle | 320
-- waiting | 18
```

miko: request rate down a bit after throttling experiment: 30% fewer write requests. errors reduced from 1.2k/min -> 200/min. still above baseline.

support-bot: PagerDuty: acknowledgement by miko at 1968000020. Escalation to cheng at 1968000040 for overlap.

cheng: verifying long-running queries: found a handful of `INSERT ... SELECT` from analytics job running every 5m. Killed the one holding locks (`pg_terminate_backend(pid=5421)`) to free the slot.

miko: customer impact: brief window ~10m with elevated errors; primary mitigation reduced failures by ~85%. Planning post-incident follow-up: enforce connection pool guidelines in SDK and add guardrails in router to backoff spiky bursts.

jamie: next steps: 1) capture slow query samples (pg_stat_statements snapshot), 2) add alert to detect `reserve_pool` exhaustion, 3) run load-test to reproduce churn.

olivia: I'll clean up redis TTL anomalies and add circuit-breaker to app cache fallback to avoid cascading db hits.

miko: handing off monitoring to cheng for the rest of the oncall window. cheng: can you keep an eye for 30m and then close the PD incident when stable?

cheng: will do. current metrics look stable. 95%ile p99 latency for writes down from 1.8s -> 350ms. errors steady ~150/min. continuing watch.

miko: thanks all. filing incident postmortem template in #incidents and tagging owners. leaving notes: runbook ref: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/db-conn-exhaust

cheng: pagerduty: incident 8921 acknowledged & being monitored by cheng. planning to close if metrics remain steady for 30m. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident 8921 status: acknowledged -> monitoring.

support-bot: Notifying customer success for top affected tenants to pre-empt support tickets.

miko: closing oncall thread, handoff complete. good work team. :slightly_smiling_face:
